The Safety and Support Conversation Checklist

What to map, notice and ask while your mother's week is running smoothly.

Download PDF

Your mother is doing fine at home, and the help around her has settled into a routine nobody ever wrote down: your sister's Tuesday drive, the neighbor who looks in most mornings, your Sundays. This checklist is for a week when nothing is pressing. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to get to when there's time, and it says nothing about how your mother is managing.

Map

Notice

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you write down, notice and ask. It doesn't say whether the help around your mother is enough, whether her home is safe, or whether anything should change. Those are questions for the professionals who assess her.

Ready for the next step?

You've mapped who helps, noticed a few things and asked the people involved. The care interview walks you through your mother's situation area by area, so the parts nobody thought to write down get asked about too, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Create Your Free Family Care Profile ›

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow AARP's planning guide for families, which says to plan with the person the plan is about and to ask the people who help about their preferences. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.
